q.chamber_basics.q1.prompt: A chamber has 12 serving members and 2 vacant seats. How many members must be present for quorum?
q.chamber_basics.q1.a: Seven — a majority of whoever attended the last session
q.chamber_basics.q1.b: Seven — a majority of ALL serving members
q.chamber_basics.q1.c: Eight — two-thirds of the serving members
q.chamber_basics.q1.explain: Quorum is a majority of ALL serving members (Art. II §2). Vacant seats are not serving members, and past attendance never enters the arithmetic.
q.chamber_basics.q2.prompt: What does a supermajority act require?
q.chamber_basics.q2.a: Two-thirds of the members present and voting
q.chamber_basics.q2.b: Two-thirds of members present, once quorum has formed
q.chamber_basics.q2.c: Two-thirds of ALL serving members — a member who stays away counts the same as a no
q.chamber_basics.q2.explain: Art. VII counts the whole serving roster, never just the room. That is why absence can never be used to cheapen a supermajority.
q.chamber_basics.q3.prompt: How is your vote on a bill actually cast?
q.chamber_basics.q3.a: By filing the floor-vote form (F-LEG-004) — every chamber vote is a public act on the record
q.chamber_basics.q3.b: By telling the speaker, who records the tally
q.chamber_basics.q3.c: By secret ballot, like an election
q.chamber_basics.q3.explain: Chamber votes are public constitutional acts — F-LEG-004 on the audit chain. Ballot secrecy protects ELECTIONS; representation is exercised in the open.
q.running_elections.q1.prompt: Which counting method do elections use?
q.running_elections.q1.a: Proportional STV with the Droop quota — never first-past-the-post
q.running_elections.q1.b: Whoever gets the most votes wins
q.running_elections.q1.c: Whatever method the board prefers for that election
q.running_elections.q1.explain: Art. II §2 hard-codes STV with the Droop quota. It can only ever be replaced by a MORE proportional method — never by plurality.
q.running_elections.q2.prompt: How many seats may a single district race carry?
q.running_elections.q2.a: Any number the map drawer likes
q.running_elections.q2.b: Five to nine — a legislature above nine seats subdivides into districts
q.running_elections.q2.explain: The 5–9 band is a DISTRICT rule (Art. II §2). A chamber's TOTAL has no ceiling — Earth seats 1,999 across 282 districts.
q.running_elections.q3.prompt: What actually seats the winners after a count?
q.running_elections.q3.b: The board's certification (F-ELB-004) — seating follows it automatically
q.running_elections.q3.explain: Certification is the constitutional act; auto-seating rides it. The oath (F-LEG-001) accepts a seat certification already created.
q.executive_basics.q1.prompt: How does a new executive normally begin?
q.executive_basics.q1.c: Delegated by the legislature — direct election comes later, and only by supermajority
q.executive_basics.q1.explain: Art. III: every executive starts legislature-delegated. Converting to direct election takes a dual supermajority — the chamber's and the constituents'.
q.executive_basics.q2.prompt: What must happen before an executive order takes effect?
q.executive_basics.q2.a: Its scope is validated against the office's delegated powers — before issuance, not after
q.executive_basics.q2.b: Nothing — orders are immediate and unreviewable
q.executive_basics.q2.explain: F-EXE-005 runs pre-issuance scope validation. An order outside the delegated scope is refused with its citation, not issued and litigated later.
q.executive_basics.q3.prompt: Emergency powers can last at most…
q.executive_basics.q3.a: As long as the emergency lasts
q.executive_basics.q3.b: 90 days per declaration or renewal — and expiry is automatic
q.executive_basics.q3.explain: Art. II §7 sets the 90-day ceiling; CLK-03 expires them automatically. Renewal of an already-expired power is refused.
q.department_basics.q1.prompt: How long is a governor's appointment?
q.department_basics.q1.b: Ten years — in lockstep with judicial appointments
q.department_basics.q1.explain: Civil and judicial appointments share the ten-year term (Art. II §9, Art. IV §1) and move in lockstep — neither can drift alone.
q.department_basics.q2.prompt: A department rule you implement (F-BOG-001) must…
q.department_basics.q2.a: Stay inside the department's delegated scope
q.department_basics.q2.c: Be countersigned by every governor on the board
q.department_basics.q2.explain: A department implements within the scope its creation act delegated. Outside that scope, the rule is refused with its citation.
q.bench_basics.q1.c: Appointed — a judiciary is appointed by default, for ten years
q.bench_basics.q1.explain: Art. IV §1: appointed is the default, ten-year terms, at least five judges per race. Switching to an elected bench needs a supermajority plus a constituent supermajority.
q.bench_basics.q2.a: Odd-sized, at least three judges — scaled to the case's severity
q.bench_basics.q2.explain: Panels are odd and at least three (Art. IV §4), scaling with severity; a constitutional-major case takes the whole court en banc.
q.bench_basics.q3.prompt: Can a person be tried twice for the same matter?
q.bench_basics.q3.b: No — double jeopardy is barred at the filing gate itself
q.bench_basics.q3.explain: The second filing is refused before any case opens — the bar lives at the validator, not in a judge's discretion.
q.advocacy_basics.q1.prompt: Filing a case for a client uses…
q.advocacy_basics.q1.a: F-ADV-001 — the advocate files on the client's behalf, on the record
q.advocacy_basics.q1.b: A private letter to the presiding judge
q.advocacy_basics.q1.explain: F-ADV-001 opens a case on a client's behalf; everything an advocate does is a filed, citable act on the docket.
q.advocacy_basics.q2.prompt: Motions, evidence and briefs may be filed…
q.advocacy_basics.q2.c: Inside the case's attach window, onto the docket
q.advocacy_basics.q2.explain: F-ADV-002/003/004 ride the attach-window gate — the docket is complete when the window closes, so nobody is ambushed at the bench.
